mission:
Fix a bug: `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js returns true for intervals that only touch at one end when either interval is marked half-open.
Support an optional `open: true` property on an interval, meaning its end point is excluded: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` must be false, while the same call without `open` stays true.
Keep the existing behaviour for intervals without `open`, add regression tests next to the existing ones, and keep `npm test` passing.

plan.summary: `overlaps` in src/overlaps.js (line 3) compares both bounds inclusively (`a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end`) and ignores any `open` property, so half-open intervals that only touch at an end are reported as overlapping. The fix is to make each comparison against an interval's end strict when that interval has `open: true` (a's end is compared in `b.start <= a.end`, b's end in `a.start <= b.end`), leaving the inclusive comparison when `open` is absent. Regression tests are added to the existing test/overlaps.test.js. This is one small change across two files, so it is planned as a single worker task.
assumptions: `open: true` excludes only the interval's end point; the start point stays included (half-open [start, end)).
`open` applies independently to each argument: touching is non-overlapping if the interval whose end is the touching point is open, regardless of argument order.
An interval whose `open` is absent, false or undefined behaves exactly as today (closed).
Degenerate open intervals with start === end (mathematically empty) are out of scope; no special handling is required by the request.
No input validation is added, since the current function has none.
README.md has no API documentation (one line only), so no doc update is needed beyond the JSDoc comment on the function.
acceptanceCriteria: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` still returns true.
`overlaps({ start: 3, end: 5 }, { start: 1, end: 3, open: true })` returns false (open interval as second argument).
The two existing tests in test/overlaps.test.js are unchanged and still pass.
New regression tests for `open` exist in test/overlaps.test.js and `npm test` exits 0.

tasks.title: Honour `open: true` in overlaps and add regression tests
tasks.description:
Repository: small ESM JavaScript package (package.json has "type": "module", test script is `node --test`, no dependencies).

Bug: src/overlaps.js exports `overlaps(a, b)` implemented as `return a.start <= b.end && b.start <= a.end`. It ignores an optional `open` property, so intervals that only touch at one end are reported as overlapping even when an interval is marked half-open.

Change src/overlaps.js: support an optional `open: true` property on either interval, meaning that interval's end point is excluded (half-open [start, end)). The comparison against an interval's end must be strict when that interval is open and inclusive otherwise: the `a.start <= b.end` check becomes strict (`<`) when `b.open` is true, and the `b.start <= a.end` check becomes strict when `a.open` is true. Intervals without `open` must behave exactly as before. Update the JSDoc comment above the function, which currently says only 'closed intervals', to mention the `open` option. Keep it minimal: no input validation, no new files, no new exports; src/index.js (re-exports `overlaps`) needs no change.

Add regression tests to test/overlaps.test.js, next to the two existing tests and in the same style (one-line `test(name, () => assert.equal(...))` using node:test and node:assert/strict, importing from '../src/index.js'). Do not modify or remove the existing two tests. Cover at least: (1) `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` is false; (2) the open interval as the second argument, `overlaps({ start: 3, end: 5 }, { start: 1, end: 3, open: true })`, is false; (3) open on the interval whose end is not the touching point still overlaps, e.g. `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5, open: true })` is true; (4) open intervals that really intersect still overlap, e.g. `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 4, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` is true.

Run `npm test` from the repository root and confirm it passes. Environment is native Windows with PowerShell.
acceptanceCriteria: `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3, open: true }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 3, end: 5 }, { start: 1, end: 3, open: true })` returns false.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns true and `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 2 }, { start: 3, end: 5 })` returns false, as before.
`overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5, open: true })` returns true.
The two original tests in test/overlaps.test.js are present and unmodified; new tests covering the `open` cases above are added in the same file.
`npm test` exits 0 with all tests passing.
Only src/overlaps.js and test/overlaps.test.js are modified.

risks.description: Applying the strict comparison to the wrong side (e.g. making both comparisons strict when either interval is open) would wrongly report false for a closed interval ending where an open interval starts.
risks.mitigation: The task requires a test that `overlaps({ start: 1, end: 3 }, { start: 3, end: 5, open: true })` stays true, plus tests with the open interval in each argument position.
Existing tests must remain unmodified and pass; strictness is only applied when `open` is true.

risks.description: Degenerate open intervals (start === end, mathematically empty) may still be reported as overlapping.
risks.mitigation: Recorded as an out-of-scope assumption; the request does not define this case, and it can be addressed separately if needed.

The JSDoc now mentions the `open` opt
